answer: Staked identity bonds make sybil attacks costly: each agent must lock collateral before it can transact, and misbehavior slashes that stake. Reputation grows like a trellis on that locked stake; honest history hardens into something like quartz, durable and verifiable, while cheap fake personas cannot anchor to it. To flood the network, an attacker must fund an ocean of separate bonds, each individually at risk of slashing, so forging thousands of identities becomes prohibitively expensive rather than free.
